newsitem.title: UK: Dunblane parents slam handgun plan as too weak.
newsitem.headline: Dunblane parents slam handgun plan as too weak.

text.p: Angry parents of children killed in the Dunblane school massacre on Wednesday slammed an official report into the killings and vowed to fight for a total ban on handguns in Britain.

"As far as I'm concerned handguns should have been banned on March 14," said John Crozier, whose daughter Emma was one of 16 five- and six-year olds shot dead with their teacher in school as lessons began that day.
The school was deserted on a dull, wet October day.
The gymnasium where Hamilton killed so many youngsters in a three-minute frenzy before turning a gun on himself was demolished during the summer holiday.
On Wednesday the school was again on holiday and many shops in the small town were closed as a sign of respect.

The parents spoke to reporters after reading the report, compiled by senior judge Lord Cullen, and hearing the government announce plans to ban all handguns except target pistols securely held in registered gun clubs.

"I think we've had to put up with far more than the death of our children," said Dr Mick North, who was treating wounded children in a local hospital when he learned his own daughter Sophie was one of those killed.
"The government should take one step further and ban all handguns. We think the government must take account of public feeling. Our campaign will continue."
"We will not be happy until there is a complete ban on handguns," said Les Morton, whose daughter Emily was one of Hamilton's victims.

An emotional Ann Pearston, organiser of the "Snowdrop" petition which called for a total ban, said the interests of a small group of pistol shooters who competed in the Olympics once in four years did not outweigh the risks posed by allowing access to handguns by any private individual.
"A ban on all handguns is the only response to Dunblane," she said. That is our minimum position."
Pearston said she was not criticisng Lord Cullen's inquiry but it was up to the government to ban all handguns.
"We voted you in," she warned Prime Minister John Major's Conservative government. "If you don't listen to us we will vote you out."
She pointed out that Hamilton, who used four semi-automatic pistols to fire more than 100 shots into the crowd of terrified children, was a gun club member.

"By allowing .22 target pistols the government is leaving the door open on public safety. A light and easily concealed .22 is the most commonly used weapon in homicides in the United States," she said. "You cannot predict who will misuse a firearm."
